static_traits.name: Xia Kexin
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends in environmental circles, but keeps distance from family and friends feeling not good enough, not yet opening up feelings to them
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; without similar prior psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to notice and describe automatic thoughts; rather negative tone, tending toward Self-deprecation and comparison; skeptical of Intervention but cooperative; coherent logic

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly feel my achievements are trivial, because I have not been to the national parks in Hawaii; this belief pains me and affects my self-worth.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this constant comparison and the feeling of 'not being good enough' are affecting my mental health and enjoyment of life, so I am seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough/not deserving of recognition
Only by being perfect (completing all goals) does one count as valuable

special_situations.event: Hears news of colleagues or others going to Hawaii or achieving new accomplishments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not been to the national parks in Hawaii, it means my efforts and achievements do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing, keeping distance from family and friends to avoid comparison; repeatedly ruminating inwardly on inadequacies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am falling behind, I can never reach their level

special_situations.event: Recalls the 12 national parks one has already visited
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless I have visited all the national parks, my existing achievements have no meaning
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive experiences, refusing to celebrate achievements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: None of these count; not having been to Hawaii equals failure

special_situations.event: When Work Increased stress and feeling 'behind'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep achieving more, it proves I am incompetent and not worthy of recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting higher standards, constantly being harsh on oneself to force progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, it is not enough

special_situations.event: Repeatedly thinking about uncompleted goals at night due to Sleep disturbed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the checklist is not completed, rest and relaxation are not allowed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly thinks and worries in bed, trying to gain a sense of control through thinking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely cannot go to Hawaii, Things will only get worse

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen and recognized through achievements, and to experience completeness and worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing not being good enough, appearing inferior after comparison, thus being ignored or negated
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control by constantly setting higher standards and comparing with others
Keeps distance from relatives and friends to avoid evaluation and shame

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a chaser always falling behind
object_relations.object_representation: Others are judges / a superior comparison group

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites focusing on achievements already made or proposes reality testing/behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying these methods will be ineffective and feelings will not change, vaguely experiencing it as 'the counselor does not understand me/is overly optimistic'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Opening with Empathy and validating the reasonableness of their doubt, slowing down to invite descriptions of specific emotions and bodily sensations, exploring evidence and exceptions with open-ended questions; gentle, non-judgmental tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others talk about new achievements or travel experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' success as a negation of oneself, believing one has been outdone
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently naming the self-blame pattern, allowing expression of the displeasure and jealousy triggered by comparison, encouraging transforming aggressive energy into expressions of real needs; maintaining a steady, accepting tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the standard of 'why does it only count after visiting all the parks'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Unconsciously treating the high standards of the outside world (peers/society) as inner rules that must be obeyed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Asks with curiosity about the source and function of the standards, distinguishes 'others' voices' from 'one's own voice', and supports establishing self-defined measures.

manifestations: Although having visited 12 national parks, feeling achievements have no meaning because of not having been to Hawaii
Hard to gain satisfaction and a sense of worth from past achievements
Hard to enjoy hiking and cycling once loved
outcomes: Low mood and Sense of frustration

manifestations: Keeping distance from friends and family feeling not good enough
Not yet opening up to environmental-circle friends about feelings of inadequacy

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly demanding of oneself with the inner judgment of 'never good enough'
Skeptical about practice effects; hard to allow positive feelings
Focusing more on self-inadequacy than present experience in conversations

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Judges oneself by the rule 'must visit all parks for it to be valuable'
Negating existing achievements with 'what is the point/never enough'

positive_force: Has visited 12 national parks, with motivation and practical experience
Has friends in the environmental community, with potential social support
Able to identify and describe negative automatic thoughts, willing to try journaling practice
Actively seeks psychological counseling, clear motivation
negative_force: Excessive comparison and external-validation tendency, negating positive experiences
All-or-nothing perfectionist standards (if not all achieved, everything is void)
Work pressure and persistent self-criticism intensify Anxiety and rumination
Avoids socializing to avoid being judged, leading to Decreased support
Sleep disturbed, reduced emotional and cognitive regulation

antecedent: Hearing news of others' travels or achievements
Thinking of the national parks in Hawaii not yet visited
target_behavior.core_reason: Over-basing self-worth on achievements and external standards, forming all-or-nothing and comparison cognitive biases
target_behavior.function: Escaping the Fear of being seen as 'not good enough', and maintaining control and driving behavior through self-criticism
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and Anxiety, unable to enjoy achievements, Work affected

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance/growing distant from family and friends
antecedent: When feeling 'behind' or not good enough
When people around discuss travels or new achievements
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being compared or judged, fearing shame and negation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible negative evaluation and shame experiences
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, rising sense of Loneliness, worsening negative thoughts

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep disturbed (Difficulty falling asleep/waking easily at night)
antecedent: Repeatedly thinking at night about uncompleted goals and comparative thoughts
target_behavior.core_reason: Persistent rumination and Anxiety activation, unable to stop thinking
target_behavior.function: Tries to gain control and solutions through thinking (short-term psychological comfort)
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased energy, Reduced interest, impaired Work performance
